Subject: Public snippet for DPA / Hosted API transfer & subprocessor summary

Hi Marcus / Karthik —

Acme (procurement) asked for a short, customer-facing paragraph we can put in the Hosted API console and in our procurement one-pager summarizing where customer data may flow and who our subprocessors are. They asked for something "plain and easy to paste into contracts" — so legal-friendly but not lawyer-speak.

Can you take a crack at a 2–3 sentence blurb + one-line pointer to the full subprocessor map? We need this by EOD tomorrow to include in the demo materials for their SOW review.

I've attached the current snippet (old language) and a CSV excerpt of the most common subprocessors. Happy to iterate.

Thanks —
Naomi

Subject: Re: Public snippet for DPA / Hosted API transfer & subprocessor summary

Naomi —

Draft below. Kept it short and avoided legal jargon. Left two variants (A = more customer-friendly, B = slightly more precise for procurement/legal).

Variant A (recommended for console card):
"Redwood Inference processes requests in regions you choose. To deliver low-latency inference, we route and cache limited request data transiently across our infrastructure and a small set of vetted subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, logging/telemetry vendors). See the full subprocessor map and data transfer safeguards in our DPA: [link]."

Variant B (for one-pager / procurement):
"Redwood Inference hosts and processes customer requests in the regions customers select. We may transmit transient request metadata and cached tokens to a limited set of subprocessors to support inference, monitoring, and storage. We maintain a published subprocessor list and contractual safeguards (SCCs / equivalent) — see the DPA for details and the most up-to-date map: [link]."

Quick notes on decisions:
- I avoided naming too many technical primitives (KV cache) in the public blurb; can include a technical appendix if Acme's infra/privacy team asks.
- The bracketed [link] should point to the console card + Drive doc.

If that looks good, Karthik — can you confirm the phrasing about "transient" and whether we should explicitly call out "embeddings" or any storage behavior?

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Developer UX | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 10:03 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Draft below. Kept it short and avoided legal jargon. Left two variants (A = more customer-friendly, B = slightly more precise for procurement/legal).

Thanks — both good starting points. A couple of technical clarifications to avoid inadvertent commitments in public copy:

- "Transient" is useful but ambiguous. Recommend "temporary in-memory cache" when we mean KV cache used for active sessions, and "short-term logs" when we mean telemetry — but keep the console card short, so maybe stick with "transient request data and short-term logs" in the procurement-facing line and just "transient request data" in the consumer-facing line.
- We should avoid saying we "transmit" embeddings unless we intend to commit to embedding persistence; instead: "may process embeddings in our environment or chosen subprocessors" — procurement teams often ask about retention explicitly.
- For the DPA link, we need a stable canonical URL (not a Drive folder). I'll ask legal for the final published DPA doc link.

Suggested small update to Variant B:
"Redwood Inference processes customer requests within customer-selected regions. We may temporarily store request data in memory for inference and retain short-term logs; in some cases we process embeddings and telemetry with a small set of vetted subprocessors. We publish a subprocessor map and the DPA with transfer safeguards."

I'll flag any wording that could be read as a long-term persistence promise.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Hi Ashlee —

Thanks for the quick ask. Below is the short paragraph we plan to publish in the Hosted API console and include in procurement one-pagers. Let us know if you want a slightly more detailed technical appendix.

Recommended console copy (consumer-facing):
"Redwood Inference processes requests in regions you choose. To deliver fast, reliable inference, we may route short-lived request data and limited telemetry through a small set of vetted subprocessors. The full subprocessor list and our DPA with transfer safeguards are available here: https://redwood.com/dpa."

Procurement/Legal copy (one-pager):
"Redwood Inference processes customer requests in customer-selected regions. We may temporarily hold request data in-memory for inference and retain short-term logs; in certain circumstances we process embeddings and telemetry with a small set of vetted subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring vendors). We publish a subprocessor map and contractual safeguards in our DPA: https://redwood.com/dpa (latest version)."

Attachments: dpa_plainlang_snippets_v1.docx (docx), subprocessor_map_excerpt.csv (csv)
